newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FARMERS TO HINDER BORDER CROSSINGS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FARMERS TO HINDER BORDER CROSSINGS.

text.p: Hungarian farmers' union METESZ said on Monday they plan to obstruct but not block traffic at six border crossings on Wednesday.
"At least several hundred cars will take part in the protest," METESZ leader Gyula Kosa told Reuters.

Farmers plan to slow down traffic by blocking one lane and will attempt to hinder traffic at frontiers with all neighbouring countries except Croatia by repeatedly crossing the border with their cars.
Kosa said two smaller unions have joined their protest.
The Kiskoros farmers have organised nationwide protests for the last month against the government's 1997 income and social security tax increases for individual farmers.

Last Monday they sent an ultimatum to the government threatening to block border crossings and roads to Budapest unless a demand for unconditional tax relief for farmers earning less than 1.5 million forints ($8,500) a year was met.
Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze warned the farmers that police would prevent METESZ from carrying out its threat.
Kosa said other farmers' unions which were "playing into the government's hands" did not join their action.
In a Sunday statement, METESZ described the Socialist-led government's farming programme as "the ruthlessly exploitative economic policy pursued by the anti-national liberal-Bolshevist government."
Government leaders attacked the statement on Sunday as political in tone.
Kosa said no government official had contacted them since METESZ issued its call for Wednesday's border obstructions.

METESZ is one of the smaller but more radical of Hungary's almost thirty farmers' unions which which have so far failed to establish a common stance over land ownership, distribution of subsidies and farming taxation.
